notes.title: Moving on
notes.content:
20230301
One of a kind gamers! It’s been a great couple weeks since launch! We’ve really enjoyed all the new players we’ve seen come to check out our game and we hope we were able to give you something fun to do. That being said, the number of new players is falling off quickly and we didn’t really make anything on in-game purchases, so it’s time to dream another dream! Unless we see another surge of players or sales take a major turn, all the additional features and items we wanted to add to NRG likely won’t make it. Sad? Don’t be! We feel there’s already a lot to enjoy with this game and we’ll continue to keep the servers up for online play as long as there’s any traffic there. We’re still here to fix any bugs you report through Steam or on our Discord server but otherwise, we’ll be working on our next project that we’re really excited for!

Completed

 Refine energy level and shot charge UI
 Distribute canisters more evenly to reduce clumps
 KO ticker to see who KOs who
 Zombots co-op revivals transfers 15% of points instead of current flat 100
 Music fading and skip song option


Next

 Our next game!


Thanks!
-Mac

notes.title: An update about updates
notes.content:
20230217
One of a kind gamers! So, we know it doesn’t look like it from the lack of written updates but NRG has been updated pretty much every day since we released it a little over a week ago! Not everything has been a massive change but there’s been a mix of quality of life tweaks and gameplay adjustments like the incredibly controversial relocation of canisters to drop onto platforms most of the time instead of randomly. We had someone suggest making movement quicker so the most recent update raised agility. Thank you all so much for your feedback to help us make this game as good as it can be, keep it up! Expect many more refinements and a few more additions over the coming weeks.

Completed

 Tons of bug fixes and gameplay refinement
 Own shots don’t break finishers anymore
 Canisters fall onto platforms most of the time instead of random distribution
 Shots don’t roll as much on the ground, reducing ground snipes

 Shot drag removed, gravity increased (need to arc shots more now)
 Co-op leaderboards now reflect individual scores, not combined
 Zombots numbers tweaked, but they always are
 Energy level and shot charge UI

notes.title: Did you miss us?
notes.content:
20220828
One of a kind gamers! We felt like we had gotten NRG to a place where it was time to try to begin marketing it, so we did. It was doing okay but we began to feel like if we did one more pass to refresh visuals and just refine the overall experience a bit more, it might go a long way. So, we’re back! We plan to drop about another month into the process to polish things up one more time before really letting this thing out to see what it can do. If it gets a decent response, we’re going to stay committed to it to introduce all the extra features we have planned but if just a handful of people love it, we’re going to move on to the next game we’ve already begun developing which we hope really knocks your socks off! We’ll see what fate holds.

notes.title: Ability quantified
notes.content:
20220612
One of a kind gamers! There’s something that we always strive for while making games and that is to provide short, medium and long-term gratification from playing them. Cool looking effects can make the seconds fly by, the thrill of winning a game can make you lose track of minutes, but what can make hours and even days drift away? Ranked matches! Watching that little number next to your name grow as you win. Plus, getting grouped with others around your skill level should help keep battles competitive while you try to keep getting better. We’re still working out the details and trying to make it as balanced as possible but it should be pretty tight by the end of next week. Hope to see you climbing the ranks!

notes.title: Not breaking the streak
notes.content:
20220206
Not breaking the streak
One of a kind gamers! Have you ever done something every week for like… a year and a half or something… and you can’t imagine just skipping it for a week? Welcome to this week’s update! Typically we like to focus on one item at a time and knock it out before moving onto the next thing but we were working on the new Forest world, then we transitioned to Zombots, now we’re reformatting the whole online matchmaking system. I blame management, but there’s hope! The new online system should be wrapped up by the end of next week, and the new Forest world shouldn’t take too much longer. Zombots is coming along but it’s going to need some more time to feel completed. Something’s just missing with it at the moment but we’ll find it! So, given this update was just a whole bunch of fake news, how are ya? Everything going well in your life? Are you on your way to the best version of yourself? We hope so!

notes.title: Knowing is half the battle
notes.content:
20220109
One of a kind gamers! We’ve learned a few things on our journey through game development and probably the most important one is that no one looks at tutorials. There are precious moments between when someone decides to give your game a shot and when they might quit if they don’t know what to do. How do you get around that? Integrated tutorials! Have the game detect how the player could be playing better and give suggestions.It’s quite a bit more work but it’s probably the best chance a game has to get people to keep learning. We hope ours helps you play your best! In more aesthetically pleasing news: white and black are now available color options on maxed-out clothes. Sound cool? Looks even cooler!

Outfits, though! Now you can create different clothing and move combinations and swap between them more easily than having to disable and enable them individually. One of a kind gamers! For months now we’ve felt like movement in general in this game could be cleaner but it was kind of just in the “good enough for now” zone. Well, we’re thrilled to announce that we finally prioritized it and getting around stages is tighter than ever! No more weak jumps up slants, no more flat kick-offs, no more seemingly random hesitations… There’s not a lot left that we feel is in need of improvement! The Solo game mode stage is probably the best one we’ve ever built but the medium and large stages could definitely use a bit more love. We also added a bit more screen pizzazz to hopefully spice things up a bit more for you and also let you know when you lose and gain energy! Wishing you the best holiday season you could ask for!!

notes.title: It’s beginning to look a lot like dopeness
notes.content:
20211219
One of a kind gamers! So, we could technically release the factory world overhaul already but from our experience, it’s a bad idea to update with such big changes right before a weekend when our lead developer is off. So many unforeseen issues arise and we have to revert to the previous build anyway. What does that mean? Buckle up for early next week! notes.title: Shots, shots shots shots
notes.content:
20211128
One of a kind gamers! Shots. We updated the shots! Interestingly, reducing their collision area was a last-minute toss-in change that ended up being the best change. We had no idea how accustomed we’d become to them registering hits from much too far away! Well, it’s a thing of the past now and the game is far better for it. Along with that, we also allowed more powerful shots to go through weaker shots so people can’t quick-shot your lethal projectile so easily, and they’re no longer stopped by canisters! Also some visual touches like them sparking off surfaces and the energy ball that’s fired being based on its charge amount. What does it all mean? Much improved combat! Also cleaned up some annoying platform glitchiness. What does that mean? Much improved platforming!
